newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures close up on short covering.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures close up on short covering.

text.p: CME lumber futures reversed early losses after finding technical support and finished strong on local short covering and fund buying, traders said.

Pressure from weather-reduced demand for cash lumber and easing cash prices gave way to short covering which boosted prices into buy stops. Expectations are that demand for wood will increase once the weather clears and dealers start to build stocks for the spring home building season.
Prudential Securities bought after the initial break which prompted local short covering. LIT division of First Options was a late buyer, they added.

Cash prices currently remain weighed down by bitter cold and snowy weather over much of the country. Wholesalers lowered asking prices another $5 to $6 per thousand board feet overnight Wednesday to the $380 to $385 area. This compares with Wednesday's official quote of $400, cash sources said.
Lumber closed 0.520 per tbf higher to unchanged with March up most at $415.50 and May up $4.00 at $386.50 per tbf.
